page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding an 8 GB per core memory ratio. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, the instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-assisted virtualization, AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic extensions. The instance does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25%, and Geekbench multi-core scores are in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with read-only large block bandwidth at 31.35 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 22.01 GB/sec. Text processing and single-threaded compression tasks perform at average levels, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput register in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highmem-2 offers a low-cost entry point to dedicated AMD EPYC resources with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. The primary tradeoff is the limited compute capacity of a single physical core, which constrains parallel processing, software compilation, and ray tracing. Consequently, this instance is best suited for memory-sensitive but compute-light workloads, such as basic caching, lightweight single-threaded applications, and small-scale text processing tasks that require more memory than a standard general-purpose instance provides.
